steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease and flour a 9x5 inch loaf pan.

In a large bowl, stir together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and white sugar. Stir in eggs, applesauce, bananas and vanilla extract. Fold in raisins and nuts if desired. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake in preheated oven for 45 to 60 minutes, until a knife inserted into center of the loaf comes out clean.

raw_recipe.headline: Granny's Banana Bread
raw_recipe.description: Very moist banana bread containing applesauce and spiced with cinnamon and nutmeg. Raisins and walnuts are optional.
raw_recipe.name: Granny's Banana Bread

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease and flour a 9x5 inch loaf pan.

In a large bowl, stir together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and white sugar. Stir in eggs, applesauce, bananas and vanilla extract. Fold in raisins and nuts if desired. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake in preheated oven for 45 to 60 minutes, until a knife inserted into center of the loaf comes out clean.

review.reviewBody: This was great. i made this for a track team dinner and everybody loved it. i used only 3/4c of sugar, and left out the nuts and raisins, but added chocolate chips. everybody wants the recipe now! oh, i would recommend only baking for 35 min... or at least checking it after that long so it doesn't overcook.

my children and I made this. it's super yummy! we left out there nuts and raisins and added in 1/4 teaspoon allspice. we made muffins with it though so we only cooked it for 30 minutes. we also doubled the recipe and it made 12 regular size muffins and 6 giant muffins.

These are awesome! Very quick and simple to make and so delicious! You could add pretty much anything to them to make them your own and they'd be fabulous. I made them into muffins. Same temp but put them in for only 30 minutes. Came out beautiful and perfectly golden brown on top! Also, I doubled the spice's as other reviewers suggested and highly recommend it.

Hello Everyone: I made this bread today. I doubled the spices and I am glad I did. The bread does not have much depth of flavor without them. I put in five small very ripe bananas and added one tablespoon of olive oil. Also, I used two cups of white flour and 1/4 cup of whole wheat flour. Otherwise, I left the recipe as is. I did not think the bread was as gummy as some reviewers indicated, just ever so slightly. I baked the bread at 350 degrees instead of 375 degrees so the top of the bread and sides in the pan did not get too done/brown during the baking process. I added the walnuts but not the raisins (because we are not fans), but I can see where the raisins would add some sweetness missing from the bread. It quite raised nicely and overall I enjoyed the recipe so I am going to keep it with a few modifications for future loaves.

Recipe was great. For those who said it was spongy, you are over mixing. Quick breads are typically meant to be stirred only till all dry ingredients are moist. I use a whisk to mix the dry ingredients together. And then stir setting on my mixer to incorporate wet ingredients.

I just made this recipe, pretty close to how it says to: only changes I made were only using 2 bananas (it's all I had), and I used a heaping 1/2 c. of applesauce. I baked it at 350, because almost every time I use my loaf pan, whatever's inside it gets too crispy on the edges (it is a dark pan). It was in there for 45 minutes (covered with foil for the last 30 minutes) and when I pulled it out, the bottom 1/3 of the loaf was still a little bit undercooked, while the sides and and bottom touching the pan were already a bit too dark (I know from experience that all this is because of my pan). The actual main part of the loaf looked great though. I tasted a piece of the loaf and it was pretty good! But I put it back in, lowered temp to 325 and will cook for 10-15 more minutes, still foil-covered, so hopefully the bottom will finish. Sorry this is so wordy. I just felt like I had a lot to explain, ha, but this really is a great recipe! I didn't give it a perfect 5 because I thought that wouldn't be fair since I did not follow the recipe exactly. :)

This bread was definitely missing salt !! It only took about two bites for me to notice it. In addition, I used half brown sugar and half white. and it gave the bread a lot more taste. I baked mine at 350 degrees for 40 minutes then reduced the temperature to 325 degrees and continued baking another 15 minutes. That change kept it from being gummy inside. Had to make too many changes for it to be the right recipe for me.

I have been making this bread for the past couple of years. It is really good. I have been using half regular flour and half whole wheat and it comes out tasting really good. Walnuts are a great addition! Last year I added chocolate chips and that was really good also. Tip- fill your muffin tins slightly above 3/4 full and they come out perfect.

I LOVE this recipe! Like many people, I vary the ingredients. Since my husband and I love dark bread, I use brown sugar instead of white. I also use VERY ripe bananas. Leave them in the fridge for about a week or two until the rind is black. It makes the bananas much sweeter. Rather than applesauce, I use apple butter. Using fresh-grated nutmeg will make your house smell heavenly while the bread is baking. This is also perfect for turning into fruitcake. Along with the raisins and nuts, add a cup of fruitcake mix to the batter. If you add fruitcake mix, it will definitely have to bake for a full hour because the batter will be dense.

Okay. So, I wanted to add a little fat to this just for my baking preferance.
I doubled this, cut out half the bananas and used one stick butter and one stick margerine and added a little salt. I used my own homemade crockpot applesauce and just a little apple pie spice, as my applesauce was already spiced up. Everything else I kept the same. The smell of this while baking was incredible. I won't be trying this myself as these will be gifts, but I'll update this recipes as soon as I hear how my friends liked them. This recipe made two large loaves and one mini, when doubled.

I loved this recipe! I changed it a little adding more cinnamon, chocolate chips and pecans (no raisin or walnuts). It has a great spicy banana flavor with my personal favorite -CHOCOLATE! This bread was gone from a party in 30 minutes - with people asking for the recipe! I did use two pans and baked for only 40 minutes. I cannot say it enough - I really love this recipe!!!
Super easy to make - many thanks
The bread turned out hard I believe due to the temp being too high. It had no flavor and not moist at all. Would not make again..

This turned out pretty good. As usual I didn't have exactly what I needed so I improvised. Results were good, but I think the original recipe would have had an edge up on my bastardization 😁. Give it a try and save yourself from the added fat in most recipes for breads and cakes.
I made this three times and was eaten within a day!

It's edible, but definitely not my favorite.

Made a very, very dense loaf that's very chewy, probably because there's no fat in it.

Recipe adjusted for 9 servings and I modified the total sugar to 1/4 c white sugar and 1/2 c dark brown sugar. I also used 1 egg + 1 1/2 Tbsp. egg substitute.

This is the first banana bread recipe I've ever read that included vanilla so I decreased the vanilla to 1 tsp. It could easily be omitted.

I did add the walnuts and raisins.

Good tasty recipe. It probably would have been better for me to mash the bananas before adding to the the batter. I'd recommend half the nutmeg, and personally I'd be good with half the sugar, but I don't like things too sweet.
I eliminate sugar entirely. it tastes great. Natural sweetness comes from the bananas. Raisins also adds sweetness. And I always include walnuts.

This banana bread is so easy. I followed the recipe except that I didn’t measure the raisins or walnuts. It was perfect. I’d like to make more than one loaf but it’s hard to keep bananas from being eaten in my house

I made this today. Followed the recipe exactly, and the loaf looked beautiful when it came out of the oven. However, that's where the positive part ended. It had an off taste, and the texture wasn't right. I think that's from using applesauce instead of oil, but whatever the reason, I won't be making it again.
